name: Turkey Bolognese Penne
intro_html: A big pot of hearty, saucy bolognese over high-protein penne, made lean with ground turkey. This is the weeknight pasta that tastes like Sunday, holds up beautifully in the fridge, and keeps you full without a food coma. Simple ingredients, big comfort, about ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost).
ingredients_display: Marinara Sauce (Great Value): 4 1/3 cups (24 oz each) (1076 g)
Parmesan Cheese (Great Value): about 7/8 cup grated (98 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Penne Pasta, 7 1/4 cups (14.5 oz each): ~$1.54. Buy 2 16oz boxes: $1.94.
Marinara Sauce, 4 1/3 cups (24 oz each): ~$2.77. Buy 2 24oz jars: $3.50.
Parmesan Cheese, about 7/8 cup grated: ~$1.18. Buy 1 8oz tub: $2.74.
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper): ~$0.13. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $23.73 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.70 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $31.34 across 14 servings, roughly $2.24 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $9.65 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $40.99. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a from-scratch bolognese. Swap in ground beef if it is cheaper that week, the macros barely move.
shop_smart: Turkey or beef, whichever is on sale. Both work here. Buy the cheaper one and freeze extra in one-pound packs.
Double the sauce, freeze half. The sauce freezes great, so a little extra effort now buys you a head start on next week.
Store-brand parmesan is a fraction of the name brand and disappears into the sauce anyway.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the penne to al dente per the box, then drain.
Dice the yellow onion, carrots, and celery fine. Warm the olive oil in a large pot and sweat them with the minced garlic until soft, about 8 minutes.
Push the vegetables to one side, add the ground turkey, and brown it, breaking it up as it cooks. Season with the salt and black pepper.
Pour in the pasta sauce and simmer 10 minutes to let it thicken into a bolognese.
Add the drained penne and stir to coat, then fold in the parmesan off the heat.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container. Every bowl lands near {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.

Marinara Sauce, 4 1/3 cups (24 oz each) (1076 g)

steps: Boil the penne to al dente and drain.
Sweat the diced yellow onion, carrots, and celery with the garlic in the olive oil until soft.
Add the ground turkey, brown it, and season with the salt and black pepper.
Add the pasta sauce and simmer 10 minutes to thicken.
Stir in the penne and fold in the parmesan off the heat, then divide into 14 containers.
